extracted.intended_audience: readers of Renaissance satire / authors designing satirical utopias
extracted.subtask_description: Extracting or using the prescriptive rules and social criteria Rabelais gives for the fictional Abbey of Theleme — i.e., guidelines for composing a satirical utopian religious order and its membership, life, and provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cardinal rule: 'Do What Thou Wilt'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This single clause governs all: liberty is trusted to produce virtue because free, well-born, well-bred persons 'have naturally an instinct and spur that prompteth them unto virtuous actions.' The text argues that compulsion fosters vice, while freedom encourages laudable emulation (if one says 'Let us drink' or 'Let us play', others follow).

rubrics_metrics.name: No enclosing walls about the convent
rubrics_metrics.description: You must not build a wall about your convent; where there is mur before and mur behind, there is store of murmur, envy, and mutual conspiracy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Physical openness is a moral design choice: walls breed murmur and envy. The abbey should be open to avoid the social ills associated with enclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: No clocks or regulated hours
rubrics_metrics.description: There should be neither clock nor dial, but according to the opportunities and incident occasions all their hours should be disposed of; 'the greatest loss of time that I know is to count the hours.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reject ritualized timekeeping and bell-driven schedules; residents use personal judgment and discretion for waking, eating, work, and sleep to avoid the 'dotage' of guiding life by bells.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selectivity of admission — physical and social fitness
rubrics_metrics.description: Into this religious order should be admitted no women that were not fair, well-featured, and of a sweet disposition; nor men that were not comely, personable, and well conditioned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contrast to contemporary convent practice of admitting the infirm or socially marginal. Thelemites should be aesthetically and socially pleasing — the rule prescribes admission based on comeliness and disposition rather than infirmity or misfit status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gender-mixed admission requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: There shall be no women in case there be not men, nor men in case there be not women.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prevent single-sex isolation that can foster secret relations; institutional life must be mixed-sex — the presence of both sexes is a precondition for admitting anyone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Freedom to depart at will
rubrics_metrics.description: All whatever, men or women, admitted within this abbey, should have full leave to depart with peace and contentment whensoever it should seem good to them so to do.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No perpetual vows or coercive lifelong obligations; members may leave freely and without penalty, reinforcing the institution's voluntary character.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection of traditional monastic vows (marriage, wealth, liberty permitted)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whereas the religious men and women did ordinarily make three vows, ... it was therefore constituted and appointed that in this convent they might be honourably married, that they might be rich, and live at liberty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Invert standard monastic expectations: chastity, poverty, and obedience are replaced by permission to marry, accumulate wealth, and live freely — a deliberate satirical reversal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Age limits for reception
rubrics_metrics.description: The women were to be admitted from ten till fifteen, and the men from twelve till eighteen.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit age windows for initiation into the order; this sets demographic norms for the community (note: reflects historical context and Rabelais' satirical intent).

rubrics_metrics.name: Expectation of broad education and cultural competence
rubrics_metrics.description: Every one could read, write, sing, play upon several musical instruments, speak five or six several languages, and compose in them all very quaintly, both in verse and prose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Residents are expected to be accomplished in arts, languages, and letters; the community values polyvalent learning and cultured talents as part of ideal membership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Physical and martial excellence
rubrics_metrics.description: Never were seen so valiant knights, ... so dexterous and skilful both on foot and a-horse-back, more brisk and lively, more nimble and quick, or better handling all manner of weapons than were there.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The ideal includes prowess in arms and horsemanship: bodily skill and military competence are part of the community's virtues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provision of abundant cultural, recreational, and practical amenities
rubrics_metrics.description: Facilities: tiltyard, hippodrome, theatre, natatory (swimming place), baths in three stages, gardens, labyrinth, tennis and ball courts, orchards, park with venery, butts and marks for shooting, stables, falconry, libraries in multiple languages, spacious galleries and halls.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The abbey should support a wide range of pursuits — athletic, theatrical, literary, piscatory, and aesthetic — to enable the free exercise of members' tastes and talents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opulent provisioning and stable endowment
rubrics_metrics.description: For the fabric and furniture ... he allotted threescore nine thousand crowns ... for the foundation and maintenance thereof for ever, he settled a perpetual fee-farm-rent ... exempted from all homage, fealty, service, or burden whatsoever.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Financial security and generous endowment are required to sustain the community's liberty and extravagant lifestyle without external obligation or servitude.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dress and appearance standards — coordinated, sumptuous attire
rubrics_metrics.description: Ladies and men apparelled richly; stockings of scarlet or purple, embroidered lists, taffety petticoats, gowns of cloth of gold, velvet, satin; caps with jewels and plumes; matching livery between sexes; ready wardrobes and artisans nearby.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A strong emphasis on seasonal, coordinated, and ornate dress; community identity is reinforced through appearance and the availability of skilled craftsmen to maintain attire.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion of certain character types and activities (inscription on gate)
rubrics_metrics.description: The inscription forbids: vile bigots, hypocrites, attorneys, barristers, law-practitioners, clerks, commissaries, judges, usurers, greedy and deceitful persons, drunkards, liars, cowards, cheaters, thieves, lazy slugs, envious, covetous, contentious bulls, fomenters of divisions, and those who make sale of deceits; it proclaims 'Lawsuits, debates, and wrangling' are exiled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly ban litigiousness, greed, hypocrisy, and other social poisons; the community actively excludes persons and professions associated with corruption, litigation, and avarice to preserve merriment and freedom.

rubrics_metrics.name: Welcome criteria — virtues and talents encouraged (inscription)
rubrics_metrics.description: The inscription welcomes: 'All noble sparks, endowed with gallant parts', 'lively, jovial, handsome, brisk, gay, witty, frolic, cheerful, merry', 'pure, honest, faithful, true expounders of the Scriptures ... who make it see the clearer', and 'ladies of high birth ... ingenious, lovely, proper, fair ... obliging, sprightly, virtuous'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The abbey actively invites sociable, witty, learned, and virtuous people who advance pleasure, learning, and neighbourly affection; spiritual interpreters are welcome provided they do not blind reason or propagate vice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Domestic and logistical organization — ready service and artisans
rubrics_metrics.description: Masters of the wardrobes had all raiments ready each morning and chamber-ladies could dress members 'in a trice'; nearby row of artisan houses (goldsmiths, tailors, embroiderers, etc.) supplied the community.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organize proximate artisanal infrastructure and efficient domestic service to enable members to pursue leisure and virtue without time lost to mundane maintenance.
